title: Platform engineering handoff digest — routing / auth / quotas / control plane
content:
Purpose: quick weekly handoff for the on-call and cross-subteam sync. Short, actionable items and explicit owners.

Meeting info:
- Date: 2026-08-04 (handoff for the week of Aug 4–10)
- Duration: 25 minutes (async-first, live follow-up where needed)
- Facilitator: Asha Kapoor
- Attendees / primary contacts: Ethan Chen (routing), Priya Patel (auth/identity), Liam O'Connor (quotas), Sofia Ramirez (control plane runtime), Marcus Lee (SRE liaison)

High-level highlights (tl;dr):
- Routing: rolling canary for per-route capacity gating completed on staging; saw 12% tail-latency regression at 99th when concurrency > 2k, root cause narrowed to suboptimal task queue sizing.
- Auth: short-lived token refresh flow updated; a backward-compatibility gap was found for older SDK clients (v0.8.x). Temporary shim rolled out to Dedicated regions.
- Quotas: quota enforcement refactor is in QA; quota-usage sync lag reduced from ~18s to ~3s with a batching change. Prod rollout scheduled Friday morning UTC.
- Control plane: KV cache eviction policy tuned; observed small reduction in memory churn but one customer reported 503s during heavy rollout — follow-up ticket assigned.

Deep dives / notes by area:
1) Routing (Ethan)
- What happened: Canary (routing-per-route-capacity) hit production-like load in staging and exposed 99th token latency regressions where request-paths with >8k tokens caused worker hotspots.
- Diagnosis: the per-route worker queue default was kept at 1024 tasks which under very bursty workloads creates long task queuing times.
- Short-term mitigation: lowered default queue window to 512 for canary nodes; configured autoscale trigger to start at 70% queue depth.
- Long-term: plan to implement weighted sharding by route fingerprint to better balance heavy prefix workloads (RFC drafted: PLT-2467).
- Action items:
  - Ethan to open a follow-up load test scenario that reproduces the token-heavy workload (owner: Ethan, due: 2026-08-06).
  - Add observability: per-route queue depth histograms and exposing s[99] latency by route fingerprint (owner: Marcus, due: 2026-08-10).

2) Auth / Identity (Priya)
- What happened: Token refresh endpoint now returns a new short-lived refresh token; older SDKs (<=0.8.x) assume refresh token reuse and will fail.
- Mitigation: rolled the shim in Dedicated regions to accept both patterns; SDK fixes required for hosted customers using older libs.
- Risks: potential auth storms if clients repeatedly retry on token failures; need rate-limits at token endpoint.
- Action items:
  - Priya to publish migration note + sample fix for SDKs in the developer blog and send to solutions-eng (owner: Priya, due: 2026-08-05).
  - Small rate-limit rule (100r/min per key) to be applied to token endpoints behind a feature-flag (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-08-07).

3) Quotas (Liam)
- Progress: quota enforcement refactor branch merged to staging; observed quota sync latency drop to ~3s in staging.
- Blocker: one integration test shows sporadic double-charging when requests race across multi-region replicas. Investigation points to replication timing and idempotency key handling.
- Plan: add an idempotency-check step on the quota coordinator and a short-term mutex in the coordinator hot path.
- Action items:
  - Liam to add the idempotency check and push to staging (owner: Liam, due: 2026-08-06).
  - Create canary on a small subset of Dedicated customers to validate no double-charges (owner: Marcus, due: 2026-08-09).

4) Control plane / runtime (Sofia)
- Observations: tuned KV cache eviction (LRU -> adaptive TTL hybrid) reduced memory churn by ~8% across worker nodes. However, one customer (enterprise-corp-9) reported a 5–7 minute window of 503s during a rollout of a model variant.
- Initial findings: rollout coincided with concurrent model pull and config reconciliation where the control plane temporarily over-allocated CPU on the reconciliation task leading to starvation of the inflight request processing loop.
- Short-term fix: deprioritize reconciliation tasks during heavy request windows and raise reconciliation CPU shares by default on Dedicated 4-node pools.
- Action items:
  - Sofia to attach profiling trace and narrow the exact reconciliation code path (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-08-05) — ticket PLT-2422.
  - Add a rollout-safety gate that prevents parallel model pulls beyond N concurrent pulls per node (owner: Ethan + Sofia, due: 2026-08-11).

Incidents and on-call notes:
- No new Sev1s this week.
- Sev2: customer reported 503s (see control plane note). On-call runbook was followed; mitigation applied but follow-through required before closure.
- On-call changes: rotating on-call for platform will shift to new schedule next week (Liam covering Wed–Fri). Please update PagerDuty shifts (Marcus).

Decisions made this week:
- Move token endpoint behind a conservative rate-limit and require SDKs to adopt the new short-lived refresh semantics (Priya/PM approval).
- Deprioritize non-urgent reconciliation tasks under heavy load; add CPU scheduling guardrails (SRE + runtime owners).

Parking lot / non-blocking ideas:
- Route fingerprinting experiment: use consistent hashing + token-bucket per fingerprint to handle bursty prefixes. (Ethan to prototype.)
- Explore small per-route local cache for very hot prefixes to reduce KV read pressure (engineering spike, 1 week).

Metrics snapshot (last 7d):
- avg request latency (hosted): 43ms
- p95 token latency (routing): 210ms
- p99 token latency (routing): 1.2s (spikes for heavy-token paths)
- token refresh failure rate: 0.6% (includes older SDKs)
- quota sync latency: median 3.2s (improved from ~18s pre-refactor)

Follow-ups / owners summary (short):
- Ethan: load test for token-heavy route (due 2026-08-06), rollout-safety gate (due 2026-08-11)
- Priya: SDK migration guide + blog (due 2026-08-05)
- Liam: idempotency step for quota coordinator (due 2026-08-06)
- Sofia: profiling trace + PLT-2422 update (due 2026-08-05)
- Marcus: add per-route queue histograms + coordinate Dedicated canary (due 2026-08-10)

Quick notes to self / TODOs (informal):
- Remember: when opening PLT tickets include exact kubernetes pod names and timeline. That helped debugging last month.
- Slack thread: #platform-controlplane -> link the staging trace once Sofia posts it.

Next sync cadence:
- Short async update (this doc) every Monday morning; live 30m sync on Thursday if high-severity items remain open.

Attachments / artifacts to check before next handoff:
- staging load test logs: s3://redwood-staging/logs/routing-canary-2026-08-03
- profiling trace (Sofia): uploaded to internal traces; link will be posted in Slack
- PRs to watch: controlplane/pull/412 (reconciliation prioritization), routing/pull/378 (queue window tuning)

If you pick anything up from this doc, drop a quick note in the Slack thread so we keep the handoff trace.

— Asha
